pr_body:
Closes #13601.

I tried to structure this so that there's a clear divide between gameplay logic and visuals to keep `DrawableSwell` from getting too big. `DrawableSwell` contains all of the gameplay logic and creates two `SkinnableDrawable`: the swell circle piece and the swell body. All of the individual pieces that make up the swell body are then constructed or retrieved in `DefaultSwell` / `LegacySwell`, where all visual animations/fades/changes to the swell (both the swell body and swell circle piece) also happen.

Did my best to make this look as close to stable as I could, but discrepancies are possible. 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/56885706/206882237-5fcaad2f-0af1-4571-86b4-e4572f11ffdd.mp4

issue_context.title: osu!taiko spinner skinning isn't implemented
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** still uses lazer defaults

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 
![osu_2021-06-21_21-04-28](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41866328/122766705-6edfea00-d2d4-11eb-9cdc-d7125b31936b.png)
![osu_2021-06-21_21-04-27](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41866328/122766714-70a9ad80-d2d4-11eb-92e9-cda17a7fd0eb.png)

**osu!lazer version:** master/2021.619.1

review_comments:
I'm not sure why I didn't complain about this before, but the fact that the swell body is animating the swell piece is really bothering me here. It's a weird dependency that doesn't strictly need to exist.

Proposed direction:

- Rename `ISkinnableSwell` -> `ISkinnableSwellPart`
- Remove the `mainPiece` argument from all of these
- Make all swell main pieces implement `ISkinnableSwellPart` and move their correspondent animations there
- In `DrawableSwell`, collect all `ISkinnableSwellPart` into an `IEnumerable` and every time these methods need to be called, iterate through all parts and call these methods for them

This is probably something that I'd be looking a second reviewer's opinion on, if I can get that.

I would avoid the concept of accessing via interface altogether with a set of events or bindables exposed from `DrawableSwell` instead, that are accessed by these pieces via DI. Sort of similar to the skinning flow of the spinner and generally follows the direction skinnable components take (DI'ing components and listening to bindables/events).

> generally follows the direction skinnable components take

I think you may be generalising too much here. That's not generally true, other rulesets do similar things. Compare: `IHitExplosion`, `IAnimatableJudgement`, `ICatchComboCounter`.

If `ApplyCustomUpdateState` suffices (I'm not sure it does), then sure, if it can work. But I don't know.

By "direction of skinnable components",. I mean the new direction that started from skinnable target support (e.g. skinnable HUD components). But my point is, you should be able to avoid the interface and enumeration completely by exposing events and subscribing to them from the pieces.

So as far as I understand it, this is hardcoded to match the legacy animation. We generally do not do this; the `ISkinnableSwellPart` proposal could address this if you did something like `parts.Max(p => p.LatestTransformEndTime)` to set the lifetime end instead.

I went through all your other review items, but this one is really giving me a hard time. Your proposal should definitely work in theory, but it doesn't because `LatestTransformEndTime` is not working for some reason. As a debug step I tried making things as simple as possible and just listing the transforms in `spinnerBody.Drawable` here, and it came up with 0 transforms (this explains why `LatestTransformEndTime` is not working). Do you have any idea what could be causing these transforms to not show up here? Could it be because I'm not transforming the entire `LegacySwellBody`, but only parts of it?
I would have to go and check to be sure but that sounds plausible.
Should be named `DefaultSwellBody` to match new naming convention.

Seems slightly off. Stable source says:

```csharp
            p.Transformations.Add(
                new Transformation(new Vector2(320, 240), new Vector2(320, 150), AudioEngine.Time, (int)(AudioEngine.Time + HitFadeIn * 2), EasingTypes.Out));
            p.Transformations.Add(
                new Transformation(TransformationType.Scale, 0.4F, 1F, AudioEngine.Time,
                                   (int)(AudioEngine.Time + (HitFadeIn * 2)), EasingTypes.Out));
            p.Transformations.Add(
                new Transformation(TransformationType.Fade, 1, 0,
                                   AudioEngine.Time + HitFadeIn * 3,
                                   (int)(AudioEngine.Time + (HitFadeIn * 5.5))));
```

`HitFadeIn` is 120 (constant). Easing type is presumed `None` if not specified explicitly.

This fallback looks wrong. I think there's a high likelihood of this working wrong if a beatmap skin is missing `spinner-approachcircle` but the user skin isn't (doing this in such a way will cause the texture to fallback to default classic skin rather than use the user's skin).

Should be using `ISkinSource.FindProvider()`; many usages across the repository of this pattern.
What's with all of this `HandleUserInput` state management? This looks like it's actually changing gameplay logic for some reason? Explanation would be appreciated.

The general reason why this is necessary is because `DrawableSwell`'s life is extended to make room for completion animations. Without stopping the handling of user inputs when `DrawableSwell`'s hitobject is completed (where its life would end before), there will be an overlap with hit objects that come after making them impossible to hit. I added a test specifically for this behavior as I agree it might be a bit strange.

This specific case on `Idle` state is only there for rewind support. When the hitobject is rewound from being completed/missed to being idle, we want to make sure it accepts user inputs again.
Should be `1.488f` or similar (stable seems to use `1.86f * 0.8` which is that). Should end on `0.1f * 0.8` too.

This workaround can't exist. Whatever is causing the lookup failure of the texture needs to be fixed at another level entirely in a separate pull request. Please open an issue or update the discussion with repro steps at it currently doesn't have enough info for me.
Same as above, `DefaultClassicSkin` should not be directly referenced. Also why is this falling back to  `spinner-circle` and not `spinner-warning`?

This is a workaround that I forgot to comment on. The `spinner-warning` file does not exist in the [osu!classic skin resources](https://github.com/ppy/osu-resources/tree/master/osu.Game.Resources/Skins/Legacy) for lazer, which is why I can't fall back to it. I don't know if the file accidentally got missing or if this is expected.

This is why I'm using `spinner-circle`. The texture is almost the same and can function as a replacement for `spinner-warning` when scaled down, with only the border around the spinner not matching exactly.
